question: The graph below shows the percentage of female members of parliament in five European countries from 2000 to 2012.
content:

Overall, all countries witnessed an upward trend in the proportion of female parliament members during the period, albeit at varying degrees. The country with the most marked amount was Spain, whereas The figure for The UK and Italy trailed behind at a similar percentange, with the latter exhibiting the most notable change over the years.

Germany, Spain, and Belgium had by far the largest proportion of female parliamentarians throughout. In 2000, just above 30% of the parliament was accountable for females in Germany, the result of which then hovered until 2008 before edging up by two percentage points in 2012 (33%). As for the figure for Spain, it started the period at around 26% and surged to about 37% in 2004, a figure which would then negligibly decline to 35% by 2012. Likewise, The amount of female parliament members increased notably to 35% in 2004 - up from approximately 23% in 2000. The figure was stable until 2008 before an increase of 3 percentage points in 2012, accounting for a chart-peak percentage at 38%.

Belgium and Italy, however, showed smaller percentages of women as parliament members. The former reached approximately 23% in 2012 - up from 17% from 2000 to 2004. The trend was relatively drastic for the latter, which climbed to nearly 25% in 2008 after remaining unchanged at 3% between 2000 and 2004. By 2012, the proportion of women parliamentarians accounted for 23%, eventually ending the period at an identical result as Belgium.

question: The graph below shows unemployment levels in Ireland and the number of people leaving the country between 1988 and 2008.
content:
The line graph illustrates changes in Ireland's unemployment rate and emigration figures from 1988 to 2008. Overall, both metrics experienced significant fluctuations throughout the period. The unemployment rate showed dramatic volatility, with the most pronounced decline occurring in the latter half of the period. In contrast, emigration figures remained relatively stable, with the exception of notable peaks in the early years and a sharp increase by 2008.

Examining the unemployment rate, 1988 recorded the highest level at approximately 17%. This declined to approximately 13% by 1990, then rose again to nearly 18% in 1991. Subsequently, a consistent downward trend emerged, with unemployment falling steadily to approximately 5% by 2000. The rate remained relatively stable until around 2007, when it surged sharply to reach approximately 12% by 2008.

Emigration figures displayed a contrasting pattern. Starting at approximately 40,000 in 1988, emigration rose dramatically to reach approximately 80,000 by 1990—representing the peak during the early years of the period. Subsequently, emigrant numbers declined sharply to approximately 30,000 by 1998, the lowest level recorded. From this point onwards, emigration figures fluctuated around 30,000 to 40,000 until 2008, when they increased to approximately 40,000.

question: The line graph below shows the consumption of five types of jam (strawberry, raspberry, grape, cherry and plum) between 2009 and 2014.
content:
The line graph illustrates the consumption figures, in millions, for 5 varieties of jam - strawberry, raspberry, grape, cherry, and plum - between 2009 and 2014. Overall, all varieties of jam, except for plum, enjoyed a general upward trend throughout the period, albeit at varying degrees. The most notable change was demonstrated by strawberry consumption, whereas cherry product volumes accounted for the smallest one.

Examining the market-leading varieties of jam during the period, strawberry dominated the market for most of the period. In 2009, just above 3 million units of strawberry product were purchased, demonstrating a gradual increase until 2014, climbing to a record high of 7 million. Raspberry held second position in the standings of best-selling jam varieties, accounting for around 2.8 million units consumed in 2009 and increasing slowly to 3.5 million in 2011. In 2012, raspberry consumption volumes surpassed that of strawberry and peaked at just above 5 million, from which point on demand stabilized around 5.5 million until 2014. Despite being the weakest-performing category in 2009 at half a million, grape product volumes demonstrated steady expansion until 2014, arriving in third place at about 4.5 million.

Moving on, cherry product occupied fourth position in 2009, at below 2 million. These volumes then fluctuated until 2011 before a noticeable increase to 3 million in 2012, after which demand remained stable until 2013. By 2014, there was a slight decline in cherry consumption to around 1.8 million, maintaining fourth place in product standings. Plum consumption levels, by contrast, exhibited a significant decrease. The metric stood at 2.5 million initially, which then revealed a period-by-period decline of half a million until 2014, becoming the marginal variety at nearly zero consumption.

question: The bar charts below show the number of people in Europe exposed to harmful levels of noise during the day and at night in rural and urban areas in 2007.
content:
The bar charts compare the number of individuals exposed to harmful levels of noise in Europe, both during the day and at night, across rural and urban regions in 2007. In general, the effect of noise pollution was significantly greater in cities than in the countryside. Furthermore, the number of people exposed to harmful noise levels — regardless of region — was consistently higher during the daytime than at night. Traffic was the main driver of noise pollution in both urban and rural areas, while industry was the least significant source.

Traffic appeared to be the leading contributor to noise pollution in cities, accounting for 68 million and 48 million affected urban dwellers during the day and night respectively. The figures dropped considerably when the impact of trains was recorded, with trains responsible for 10 million individuals during the day and 8 million at night. The number of those exposed to harmful noise levels due to aircraft fell further, to 4 million during the day and 1 million at night, while industry was the category with the fewest affected city dwellers, at 1 million during the day and a quarter of that figure at night.

In contrast, figures were noticeably lower in rural areas. Traffic remained the primary cause of noise pollution, with 35 million daytime and 24 million night-time affected individuals. These numbers dropped by almost a third when train-related noise was recorded, registering 8 and 6 million people during the day and night respectively. The least impact was seen from aircraft-related noise, with figures of 2 million during the day and 1 million at night, while industry showed no individuals exposed to noise above healthy levels in the countryside.

question: The plans below show a college café before and after its redevelopment.
content:
The maps illustrate the layout of a college café before its redevelopment in relation to its current state.

Overall, the café has undergone notable modifications to several facilities. Internally, new amenities have been introduced, including a salad bar, coffee bar, staff dining room, and recycling bins, while an outdoor barbeque area with seating has been constructed externally. These enhancements have made the café more user-friendly and visually appealing.

Prior to redevelopment, the café featured a kitchen on the upper left-hand side, which housed a serving area for food and drinks overlooking the main hall. Tables and chairs were positioned in the central area of the building. Two staff dining rooms occupied the northern side, while toilets were situated in the right-hand corner. Entry to the café was from the northeast, with a bin located immediately to the left upon entering.

Currently, a dedicated hot meals section now occupies where the original serving area was located. The two staff dining rooms have been transformed into a take-away food section on the left and a coffee bar on the right. A salad bar has been installed on the western wall of the hall, while the standard bin has been replaced with recycling bins. The toilets, tables, chairs, entrance, and kitchen remain unchanged. Outside, a barbeque area is now available to the south, featuring outdoor seating arranged with a barbeque positioned on the western side of the open space. Access to this outdoor area is provided through single-swing doors positioned on both the western and eastern walls.

question: The bar chart shows the percentage of attendance for three types of music events in 2006 in Australia.
content:

Overall, among younger and middle-aged cohorts, the most favoured type of event appeared to be popular music, followed by opera and classical. In contrast, older age groups attended opera concerts more than classical and popular music events.

Starting with the youngest cohort (15–24), popular music events demonstrated the highest attendance share at 38%, which was almost three times greater than that of classical and opera music attendance (13% vs 11%). The same pattern was observed among visitors aged 25–34, with attendance accounting for 27% at popular music events, 14% at opera concerts, and 8% at classical music events. Meanwhile, those aged 35–44 shared similar patterns, albeit at higher percentages - popular music recorded 33% of total attendees, followed by 25% at opera events and 11% at classical music events.

A entirely different pattern emerged among older attendees, as opera was more popular with both age groups (45–54 and 55+) at an identical 15%. Popular music events attracted around 13% of total attendees in the former cohort, which was 3 percentage points higher than that of classical music events. In the latter cohort, these shares dropped noticeably to 8% for classical music events and to a mere 5% for popular music events.

After a decade, there had been noticeable changes in the interest of students. Despite being again the most followed course, the proportion of those attending face-to-face courses registered a decline of 10% (40%). Online lessons quickly became famous to the point where around 3.5 in tenth of students enrolled in these lessons, while the same scenario was observed for mixed-media courses, making up 20% of the total enrollments. In contrast, there was a noticeable decline to 5% in the share of correspondence courses.

In summary, in-person courses, while demonstrating a downward trend during the period, stayed the most followed type of courses, while the share of correspondence courses mirrored this trend. Other courses - online and mixed-media - appeared to turn out more popular with students over the years.

content:

Another country down the list was Korea — though it exhibited relatively smaller starting and 15-year salaries ($30,500 vs $52,600), its top salary accounted for $84,500, attained over 37 years, placing it second.

The maximum pay of teachers in the remaining countries was somewhat similar. $62,400 was the amount teachers received after working for 34 years in Japan, whose initial pay stood at $28,000 — the smallest starting salary recorded. This rose by $21,000 after serving for 15 years. The pattern for Australia and Denmark was quite identical: the pay after 15 years and the top amount for both countries remained unchanged, at $48,000 and $54,000 respectively. Despite taking only 9 and 8 years to reach top salary, teachers in these countries commenced their positions at $34,600 and $47,000 respectively.

The report focuses on the result of two surveys done to assess the aspects of living in urban places in three categories- good, bad, and none of them- at intervals of 1980 and 2010 in two tables. Units are in percentage terms.

Generally speaking, there were more people leaning towards residing in city as a favorable act of doing in both years generally compared to those who opposed to this idea, while the figures for concerns on brackets such as employment, healthcare and environments rose noticeably over the years. Additionally,the index of those who gave neutral feedback exhibited a downturn trend over the years.

In 1980, healthcare was the most favored category, with overwhelming a high of 82%, while education and environment legged behind, at 72%. By 2010, the percent of the former, however, fell heavily to 74, and being surpassed by 8 points by that of education, The index of environment kept steady, with a tiny decline to 71%. In 1980, other categories such as shops, employment and transport ranked as the most satisfying side of urban life from a low 52% by transport to 64 % in shops.

Those who had neutral perspectives about these aspects had rather lower rankings,with in 1980 the proportions being from a low 16% in transport to a high of in the bracket in education at 23%. By 2010, these relatively showed an upward trend, where transport topped the list, at 23%, and the reverse was true for employment, marking a meager 5%.

Poor feedback was also received, which seemed to increase over 30 years. In 1980, the frontrunner was transport in 1980, which in fact remained at the same position in 2010, at 32% and 38% respectively. In the first year, below 10 percent rankings were pointed to education, healthcare and environment, while the percent terms of other categories contributed to around 10%. By the second period of survey, it revised to a higher percentages, with everyone category, except chart-leader transport and a lowest low score given education(9%), recording around from 12% to 23%. well, this report was full of information, and is one of the hardest ones to write under exam conditions as time is a real hastle there. so it took 14 minutes to write it for me :)

question: The pie charts below show the percentage of household expenditure on six categories of goods and services in a European country in 1958 and 2008.
content:
The report compares percentage terms of total expenditure of individuals in a certain European country on 6 services and goods at intervals of 1958 and 2008 in two pie charts. Services and goods mentioning are housing, clothing, entertainment, food, travel or transport, and lastly luxury items.

As can be seen, over the years investing in these areas - housing and luxury items- appeared to rise at the highest volume, while people tended to allocate less money on all the other categories, among which the share of entertainment lagged far behind. Interestingly, Housing had emerged as the main priority people invested by the end of the period.

IN 1958, it was the sector of food to which money was spent the most, at staggering 32%, while following almost closely was housing, with 22%. Said that, the former bracket fell out of favor, down to a moderate of 12% in 2008, where the latter managed to reach 32%, a nominal increase of 10% from the previous year. Meantime, the proportion of expenditure on clothing remained unaltered during the years, keeping up at 18% - the third most money allocated sector.

By comparison, the figures for the three categories averaged around 10% in 1980, with spending on travel and transport making up 8%, the result of which then surged to 12%. Another such scenario was seen in the share of luxury ( making one of the highest surges in the chart), from 7% in 1958 to 17% in 2008. Surprisingly, people originally in 1958 devoted 12% of their total spending on entertainment, yet fell hugely to 6% in 2008.

question: The tables below show the number of exchange students between Europe and Australia in 2007 and 2009.
content:
The report outlines information about the volume of exchange students between Europe and Australia at intervals of 2007 and 2009 in two tables.

Generally speaking, the amount of students going to Australia rose significantly over the years across all countries, except France and United Kingdom, but the trend revised towards the opposite pattern for those going to Europe therein. While France held the highest figures for exchange students in both terms ( sending and receiving students), the index of Netherlands legged relatively behind.

Reporting the number of students who went to study to Australia from Europe, 61 in 2007 and with a mere increase in 2009 at 60, students visited Australia, topping the list. Meantime, The index of Sweden ranked the second, averaging around 34 in 2007 and 42 in 2009, wherein the same number were sent to Australia from Netherlands in both years, accounting for 36. However, the index of Germany exhibited rather most pronounced growth, hitting a high of 62 in 2009, 35 students more than the previous year. In total, the trend shoed a moderate increase to 226 in 2009, 37 students more than 2007.

In contrast, the volume of those from Australia to Europe went downwards from 2007 to 2009 across all countries, but France and Germany. The latter country provided a meager 18 students, the result of which then rose to 26, while from the former country 37 students came to Europe in 2007, and a record of 58 in 2009. The results of Sweden and Netherlands accounted 33 and 32, and then the results of those dipped significantly to 27 and 18 respectively, the latter saw the highest downfall in the second table. Moreover, the index of students from United Kingdom made up an initial of 32 and then up to 23 students.

question: The line graph below shows the number of international students from the US, the UK and Australia from 2002 to 2007.
content:
The report provisions information about the volume of international students from the US, UK and Australia from 2002 to 2007 in the line graph. Generally speaking, the leading country in the regard was the US, outstripping the number of students from UK and Australia consistently, which was followed by, however, that of The UK. At the another spectrum of the report, notably, was Australia, the figure for which legged behind, and remained unaltered throughout the period in the question.

As for the most pronounced results, the front runner was the US, with initiating at 50 000 students studying abroad. It then dipped marginally to around 47 000 in 2003, and managed to recover instantly in 2005. Till 2007, the number of American students rose to a high of 50 000. an original point where it started.

Said that, the trajectory was rather downwards for The UK international student number. Starting at a stable result of 30 000 from 2002 to 2003, it entered the period of a slight, but continuous decline towards 20 000 till 2007.

The volume of those from Australia, interestingly, was sustained during the period, from 2002 to 2007, at a trough of 10 000 - the least marked result in the graph. (202 words)

question: The bar chart below shows the bedtime activities (reading, brushing teeth, having a bath, watching TV and eating) of American children.
content:
The report focuses on the data about the involvement ratio of 5 bedtime activities - reading, brushing teeth, having a bath, watching tv and eating - done by American children in the bar graph. In general, all age bracket kids prioritize reading in their night routine over other activities, whereas eating and watching tv are considered to be the least popular ones, suggesting children in the US follow mainly a healthy and balanced night routine.

Focusing on the most preferred routine activities, reading stands out out of 5, with 1-3 years old hovering around 65, 4-5 years topping the least at 70 - the chart peak result, and lastly those aged 6-8 years marking a close 60. As for brushing teeth, it is the second favorable activity, where the youngest group accounts for the lowest at 30, followed by 4-5 year children's result averaging around 45, the result which surges further for 6-8 aged children to 50. Another such favored activity is having a bath, a trajectory of which is reverse here, with going down from 40 in the youngest to around 30 to the eldest age bracket in the chart.

Watching tv and eating are the least popular activities done by American children, amounting to below or at 20. Out of the three, only the figure for 4-5 year-old kids constitute 20, whilst other two are sustained at 15. The index of the latter is,however, rather downwards, with the sole exception of the youngest group recording 20, and the trend for 4-5 and 6-8 marking a trough of 10 - the lowest involvement ratio in the chart. question: The line graph below shows the price of four types of bread (wholegrain, brown, white and rye) in a European country between 2001 and 2005.
content:
The report outlines data on the changes in the price ratio of four bread sorts - wholegrain, Brown, White and Rye - in a country in Europe between 2001 and 2005. Units are in euros.

In general, initially being the most priced type of bread, the value of wholegrain dipped significantly over the years in the question, while that for brown rose at a pronounced rate. Interestingly, there were upwards trends in other two bread sorts too, with the market value of white being relatively higher than Rye.

In 2001, the most expensive bread was wholegrain (0.8), whilst the three stood at exactly 0.6. The result of latter was upwards with the noticeable price growth till 2002 - a chart-peak result at 1.8, before finally halving all the way down to 0.8 in 2005. From an initial 0.6, the brown quickly surpassed that of the two, to a high of 1.5 in 2002, and oscillated at 1.6 till 2005.

The price market of White and Rye were not as pronounced as above mentioned bread sorts, where Rye's value was priced at most around 0.7, with a mere surge over the years - from 2001 to 2005. White, in contrast to the just stated bread type, exhibited a moderate growth to 1.3 over this span. a trend that clarifies unpopularity of this bread type.

question: The bar chart below shows the percentage of total energy supplied by renewable sources in Australia, Germany, Norway and Iceland in 2000, 2004 and 2007.
content:

Overall, the leading figure in terms of renewable energy reserves was the Norway across al the years given in the question, exhibiting a further growth too, which was followed closely by Iceland. Australia, on the other hand, was the last runner in the chart, producing the least amount of alternative sources and remaining almost intact;meantime, that of Germany was a little marked, albeit with a meager growth in the supply volume.

Norway had the most significant reserve of renewable energy, far surpassing that of other countries. Starting at about 60% in 2000, it surged to a high of 80% in 2007 - the chart-peak result in the chart. Iceland, in comparison, ranked the second by nearly 10% gap. It commenced at 50% in 2000, and saw a meager growth by 10 points in 2004 before dipping to 55% in 2007.

At the another end of spectrum were Australia and Germany, both of which accounted below 20% in all years. Starting with Germany, its renewable energy reservoir constituted 12% of total supply in 2000, the result of which rose to nearly 20% in 2007, a change that explains although it had smaller proportions, it showed an increase in renewable energy supply, which was rather a positive development. However, Australia's alternative source supply was sustained in three given years, averaging around 10%.

question: The table below shows how water is used in three sectors in Australia, Canada, China, Russia, Turkey and the UK.
content:
The report outlines a breakdown of water consumption in three sectors of use across countries - Australia, Canada, China, Russia, Turkey and The UK in the table. Units are measured in cubic meters, and mentioning sectors are domestic, agricultural and industrial ones.

As can be seen, agriculture tends to be the most water demanding category, where the figures largely surpassed that of other two areas in all countries, with the amount of Russia topping the list. Distantly followed by, but in the second position, is the water channeled to industrial use among all the six, with the exception of Australia and Russia: the consumption of which was higher in domestic use, a sector that showed the least amount of water.

Focusing on the most amount of water supplied sector, the index of Russia shows the most noticeable result, amounting to 1863, while that of Canada and Turkey are also marked, with the respective figures of 1238 and 1482. The water supplement to agriculture of countries down the list remain lower than 1000, with around 800 cubic meters of water is purposed for agricultural use in UK and China, and the list closing country is Australia, at 741.

As for water usage on industrial purposes, the leading country is Canada, with 832 and coming close to this amount is Turkey, accounting for 732. 276 cubic meters of water is utilized in Australia to the same area, with UK exceeding this at 398;however, China and Russia appear not to allocate much water to industry, with 71 and 56 respectively.

Almost all countries show the least amounts of water used in domestic purposes, not counting countries - Australia and Russia — showing relatively higher amounts than the figures for industry sector, at 341 in the former and 98 in the latter. The remaining countries, in descending order, are Canada (279), Turkey (80), the UK (38), and China (26).

question: The bar charts below show the average number of hours students at five universities (A–E) spent studying on weekdays and at weekends.
content:
The report outlines the time ( in hours) each student from universities A,B, C, D and E spent studying with two separate graphs— on weekdays and weekends.

From an overall perspective, the hours of studying on workdays across all universities is sustained at similar patterns, albeit students of university C devoted slightly more time. On weekends, however, it differs, with the amount of time halving, in descending orders, from university A to university E, whereas the smallest figure is observed in university D.

Reporting figures regarding weekday-hours of studying, it is evident that there was a universal similar trend across all universities, amounting to around 10 hours. While the result of students in university C shows a peak of 10.6, it is followed by that of university B, accounting for 10.1. At exactly 10 hours, students from university E tend to study. In contrast, those from university D and A devote much smaller hours, with respective figures of 9.6 and 9.8 hours.

On Sundays and Saturdays, each university exhibited a downward trend, with the clinching top spot being credited to students of university A, at 9 hours. 8.6 hours of study is seen in the result of university B students, while by 8 points lower is university C. The hours of study dips further for the remaining university, with university E marking 6.2 hours and university D at 5.6, an amount that lags far behind compared to other universities.

question: The line graphs below show the number of men and women in prison in a European country from 1911 to 2001.
content:
The report focuses on the information about changes in the prison population in a country located in Europe from 1911 to 2001 diverted by one line graph for male numbers in prison and one for female prisoners.

Overall, there was a noticeable disparity between the number of offenders in both genders, where that of men exceeded the number of women at astonishing rates. Despite oscillating in the initial half of the period, the figure for imprisoned men showed a drastic rise in the end, amounting to the most noticeable number of offenders in custody. Meantime, the number of women serving sentences was relatively lower than that of men, starting with a radical drop in the first few years, albeit showing a minimal increase thereafter.

Focusing on the figures regarding male imprisoners, from 1911 to 1971 the figures regarding male imprisoners was sustained at around 20000, which started at just below 20 000. After this, it stood still till for a decade, and then declined moderately to a mere 10 000 before managing to recover to its original point in 1971. By 2001, the amount of men in prison reached its peak at staggering rate, up to a high of 45 000, a point where it showed its all-time-peak number.

When it comes to female offenders, it is clear that the country witnessed a huge fall in the number of female offenders over the years compared to the reverse trend for men, the result of which was at just above 3 000 and plummeted, down to a trough of 5 000 in 1941. After fluctuating around 1 000 for additional 4 decades, the result of women hit 1 800 numbers in the final year: almost 46 000 numbers less than that of men, marking a huge gap between genders.

question: The bar chart below shows the weekly spending of a family in a particular country from 1968 to 2018.
content:
The report provides information about the changes in weekly spendings of one family in a certain country over a half century ( 1968-2018) in the bar chart. Units are measured in percentage terms relative to weekly income.

Generally speaking, by far the largest expense was allocated to food items, marking the most noticeable growth over the years in the question, while it was fuel and power that closed the list. Interestingly, the only area that remained intact was the money spent on household goods during the period. With regard to other expense areas, there were slight and significant changes.

Food was the most money channeled sector at that time, The proportion of weekly expense, however, halved nearly twofold to 35% in 2018, up from 17% in 1968. Other areas with such identical changes were clothing and footwear ( 5 vs 10) and personal goods ( 4 vs 8), as the percentage of money spent on those in the latter year is significantly lower than what it used to be in the former. In contrast, the money spent on fuel and power exhibited a relatively smaller decline by 2%, initially accounting for 6% and 4% in 2018.

Areas to be mentioned below, on the other hand, experienced a growth in terms of weekly money allocation by households, with that of leisure marking the highest change from 8% in 1968 to 23% in 2018 — almost tripling its original point. The figure for housing and transport followed the same trajectory, with the former rising from 10% to 18% and the latter from 7% to 13% during the years provided.

Furthermore, the proportion of money people allocated to household goods had remained intact. In both years, it made up a moderate 7% - the only area where spending figures did not change.

question: The pie chart below shows the use of four types of transport (car, bus, taxi and LRT) in Edmonton, and the table shows the reasons people chose them.

question: The table below shows the amount of money a single person and a couple need to spend on seven categories of expenses to live comfortably after retirement.
content:

question: The line graphs below show the number of visitors from France and North America to the UK for holiday and business purposes from January to December of one year.
content:
The report outlines information regarding the volume of visitors from France and North America in terms of holiday and business reasons to The UK in one year period from January to December in the line graphs. Units are in million figures.

In general, the majority of passenger arrivals due to both holiday and business reasons was attributed to North America, which in terms of holiday visits, once peaked in July, declined towards the end of the year, whereas those from France showed a relatively stable result during the period.Outbound travel figures in terms of business, on the other hand, was similar for both countries, where they showed the highest visitor ratio in May and October, ending the period with moderate downward trends.

With regards to the number of holiday visits to the UK, quite interestingly both countries started the period at the same number, at 1 million in January. The index of France, however, followed an increasing figure till July, a point where it marked its all time-high, at 3 million, while the number of French visitors increased but negligibly to 1.5 million. At this point passenger arrivals from these countries fell significantly and converged in December, at just around 1 million — the same number as in the beginning of the year.

As for the rate of those who visited the UK for business reasons, there was a similarity in the trajectory of two countries with 0.10 million disparity in their amount. Starting at 0.25 in January, the amount of north American visitors surged towards 0.5 till May, which then halved to 0.2 before showing a continued recovery in October: it reached its peak at 0.55 million and then again declined to 0.25 million in the end of the year. Similarly, the trend for French passenger arrivals followed a suit, but with that 0.10 million gap in each month, yet it finished the period at 0.2 million — a closer amount to the former than what it previously showed.

question: The bar chart below shows three methods of waste disposal (landfill, burning and dumping at sea) in a European country from 2005 to 2008.
content:

In summary, despite being a leading figure, the result of landfilling exhibited a downturn trend over the years, while that of burning surged, eventually emerging as the most favored method to dispose waste. question: The line graph below shows changes in the price of an 800-gram loaf of four types of bread between 2001 and 2006.
content:

White was another bread sort which experienced a growth in its price in that time frame. question: The table below shows the salaries of secondary school teachers in Australia, Denmark, Luxembourg, Korea and Japan in 2009.
content:

Followed distantly, albeit at the second position, was Denmark, with starting point at 47.000, 54.000 with 15 years experience and the same at the maximum level ( 8 years to reach the top salary).

In remaining regions the salary secondary teachers received was relatively less, Australian teachers used to get paid at 34.600 when they first started, and after 15 years it rose high to 48.00, which remained unchanged in the maximum category ( reaching the peak salary took a total of nine years). For Korea, it was 4 thousand lower, at 30.500, yet it increased considerably with the experience years ( 52.600 with 15 years and after 37 years teachers received as much as high 84.500). Such a change of the salary was seen in the result of Japan too, going from the starting point of 28.000,surging to 49.000 with 15 years and a peak of 62.400 after 34 years of service — nearly twice more than the starting salary.

question: The diagram below shows the stages in the cultivation and processing of pineapples.
content:
The report confers stages involved in the production of pineapples along with their cultivation and preparation process in the diagram.

In general, manufacturing of pineapple products comprises a number of stages in the linear process, with harvesting them beginning in the nature. To ensure healthy and right growth of these fruits, a fertilizer known as Ethaline is used most importantly, once gained desirable weight and height, they are processed into ready products: it is one of the three - juice production, canned pineapples and the ones that are exported.

It all begins in the nature when pineapples are grown under the sun from 23 degrees to 30 degrees. It is vital that their crowns while growing are placed between 26 cm in a row, and after maturing for 7 months, Ethaline is purred via special tubes - a type of fertilizer that makes it sure to maintain the growth of pineapples, at which point there are more 5 months to go for pineapples to be ripe and be in the desired condition: 30 cm in height and around 2 kilos in weight.

Ripe pineapples, first of all, need to be washed, after which they journey into production, where there are three resulting products: Juice, tinned pineapples and pineapples to be exported. As for the former and latter products, they are skinned and tailed, and cores are removed. To make juice, these pineapples travel through an extractor, a device that takes out their juice before packaging. In the case of tinned pineapples, after undergoing standard preparatory procedures as juice production, they are sliced into rings. The small leftovers and ringed pineapples then go straight into tins.

As for pineapples to be exported, they proceed to a waxing process, where they are covered with wax with the use of tubes resembling rain. Placing them into crates is next until it is time for transporting to ships before making their way for exporting.

Generally speaking, the share of those living independently surged across all age groups during the period in the question, albeit at varying degrees - for instance, the most pronounced growth being shown by the eldest age cohorts,while the result of middle-aged individuals registering a moderate increase. In contrast, the fewest share of those living alone as well as the smallest growth were responsible for the figure for the youngest age cohort.

There were consistently more individuals leaning towards solitary lifestyle in the country among the eldest age demographics. In 1850, the figure for 55-64 age demographic formed around 3% of those living alone: this figure rose significantly from that point on to 9% till 1950, and to a staggering 17% in 2000. Meantime, this sort of trajectory was also echoed by the proportion of another older age cohort(47-55), though it hovered mostly around 2% and 4% from 1850 to 1950, eventually hitting a significant 13 percent in 2000.

The changes among middle-age cohorts were not as noticeable as the aforementioned ones. From 1850 to 1950, the amount of individual occupancy between 37 and 46 years old edged up from its starting point at just above 2% to nearly 3%, but the result of which upsurged modestly by 4% in 2000. The records for 27-36 age cohort was registered from 1900, where it stood at 2%, and at 3% in 1950. This age cohort also recorded a gradual increase in 2000, up to 8%.

Individual household living figures for the youngest age cohort(17-26) were the all-time lowest. The figure was first recorded in 1950 at 2%, while this figure grew up to a trough of 5% in 2000.

question: The table below shows marriage trends in one country in 1960, 1970, 1980, 1990 and 2000.
content:
The report is about figures regarding martial trends in one country in 5 years - 1960,1970,1980,1990 and lastly 2000 - in the table. The data compares information about forms of marriages, in numbers, along with the average age of brides as well as bridegrooms.

Generally speaking,religious marriages were more prevalent compared to civil ones initially, although the trend for both of which rose in the years given, at which point the figure for state-recognized marriages exceeded that of its counterpart eventually. Similarly, average age rates also followed the suit over the period, where bridegrooms tended to be a bit elder than brides did.

From 1960 to 1990, the incidence of marriages under religious rules were quite common as opposed to civil marriages, with a huge disparity. For example, in 1960 25 000 marriages were carried out in a religious way: this was almost thrice more than civil marriage(8000). The all-time high result of religious marriage rates was observed in 1980, hitting a whopping 50 000;meantime, the figure for civil ones accounted for 16 000. By 1990, figures followed different trajectories, with the religious marriage becoming less popular, and civil marriage numbers keeping up to that of the former(32 000 vs 23 000). It was only 2000 when the index of civil marriage, for the first time, outnumbered that of religious ones,registering 40 000 - 6 000 more than the latter.

During the period, it appeared that people gravitated towards the later marriage. In 1960, the age of brides averaged around 21, while bridegrooms entered a marriage life, around their 24 years old. The gap was closer in 1970 and 1980 between average age of brides and bridegrooms, with a margin of 2 years (23 and 25 vs 25 and 27 respectively). For 1990 records, the average bride age was registered at 27, and for bridegrooms it was noticeably, again, higher at 30. Finally, brides got married at their 30 as did bridegrooms at their 32 in 2000.

question: The map below shows the development of the village of Ryemouth between 1995 and present.
content:
The report outlines data regarding the transformation of Ryemouth village over a 31-year period(from 1995 to the present day) in two pictures.

As can be seen, the village has witnessed a rather significant transformation throughout the period, with its residential facilities being enhanced at a large-scale. Plus, there can be seen also overall entertainment enhancement - for instance, tennis and golf areas at the cost of the greenery, and a restaurant, while the shift in the area is evident from being industrialized to more residential-friendly.

In 1995, the access to the village was from the north-western area through the road, stretching to the beach, where the road divided and went to the east and west sides. On both left and right sides of the road in the north was where housing areas were located. Additionally, the village had a separate residential region in the square shape. Moving on the eastern side of the village, residents could access to a forest park, above of which was a farmland, while on the southern area of the village there was access to the sea. Along the beach, villagers had a fish market, on the more western area of the beach, and a cafe’, on the opposite side. In front of the fish market, a shop was situated, and in the vicinity of the intersection of the road there was a hotel. Lastly, a fishing port was in the centre region of the beach in the sea.

During the period, there have been a number of changes in the layout of the map. For example, the volume of accommodation in the village has been increased, both in the northern side and inside of the square housing area, which in fact gained an extra access from the west. The greenery, a farmland and a forest park, has been converted into tennis courts and a golf area, while the same modification can be seen where a shop used to be: it has given room for a restaurant. We also now have apartment blocks, where previously a fish market occupied, although facilities like a cafe and a hotel have remained intact - at present those visiting a hotel can enjoy a car park built next to it. The disappearance of the fish market has also resulted in demolishing a fishing port.

question: The charts below show information about water consumption in Australia in 2004 and how residential water was consumed in the same year.

content:

question: The charts below show what Australian school leavers did immediately after leaving secondary school.
content:
The chars show what Australian school leavers did immediately after leaving secondary school

The report compares the percentage points of people who were employed, unemployed and continued their education after graduating their secondary school at intervals of 1980, 1990 and 2000, as shown in pie charts.

In 1980, the lion's share of secondary school graduates leaned on pursuing their education, at 50%, with the employment rate a close second, at 40%. By contrast, only a small portion of students did not got a job as well as pursued further education, accounting for a through of 10%.

By 1990, the shares of employment and unemployment among secondary school graduates were on an upward-slope (50% vs 12%), while those who kept studying registered a decrease of 12 percentage points, to 50%.

In summary, the volume of students opting being employed after their secondary education appeared to be more prevalent over the period, while the unemployment figures hovered. Conversely, students seemed to lose their interest in pursuing further education. By far the largest share of students opted to be employed by the end of the period, while the smallest share accounted for unemployment figures consistently.

question: The chart below shows the proportion of survey respondents that showed interest in particular sports in UK.
content:
The report outlines data regarding how people responded to the survey looking at the interest rate,in percentages, in six types of sports in The U.K in the years 1995,2000 and 2005 in the bar chart. Sports in the question are golf,tennis,snooker,rugby,swimming and lastly football.

In general, interested parties were primarily drawn to football relative to other sports, which registered an overall increase during the period - the similar trend in the proportion of swimming. Apart from these two sports, the interest of participants in the survey dropped, albeit at varying degrees,among which the figure for tennis closed the list.

Football had the most significant proportion of interest figures consistently, starting at 45% in 1995 and increasing modestly till 2005, when around 50% of respondents reported they opted football than any other sports. The trend for swimming followed suit: in 1995, 25% of individuals preferred swimming,hitting its peak at 30% in 2000. This figure,however, dropped to around 27% in 2005.

For remaining sports, the figures were quite similar between 20 and 40%, fluctuating around during the years and within sports. For example, Despite showing just around 28% interest rate in 1995, actually more participants responded a preference in 2005 for rugby(30%). This was down to 25% for the interest rate of snooker in 2005, which rather had relatively more advocates back in 1995 (30%). The proportion of proponents of tennis had went down gradually by 2005 (22%): in 1995, almost 28% of respondents responded that they liked tennis. At the end of the list was golf, which had more advocates in 2005, accounting for 25%, and this was up to 27% in 1995.

question: The bar chart below shows the main reasons for students choosing to study at a particular university in the UK in 1985 and 2005.
content:
The report confers data on why students chose to study at a particular university in The U.K at the intervals of 1985 and 2005, as shown in the bar chart. Reasons students reported were teaching quality, sports facilities, degrees programs, proximity to home, and lastly resources.

Generally speaking, surveyed students were particularly drawn to the sports facilities university provided, while students were less interested in factors such as the distance to their home and resources. Notably, opinions about variety of programs in the university had not changed during the period, whereas figures for teaching quality and sports facilities were up over the years - the most significant increase in the figure for sports facilities. In contrast, the amount of students choosing other two reasons dropped.

In 1995, it was teaching quality that attracted the most number of students (22%), with degrees programs a close second (20%). Almost similar figures were seen in the percentage of proximity to home and resources (17% vs 15%). The least popular motive among students was sports facilities in 1995, around 12% students opting it.

By 2005, percentages had changed quite significantly. Sports facilities, for instance, emerged as the most popular reason why students studied at the university (27%), surpassing the figure for teaching quality, though it showed a modest increase. up to 26%. The amount of proponents who reported the variety of programs within the university remained unchanged, but students, who claimed that the distance from their home and resources were what appealed to them the most, showed less interest in 2005 (10% vs 11% respectively).

question: The bar chart shows waste collection by a recycling centre from 2011 to 2015.
content:

question: The graph below shows the types of transport used by tourists who visited New Zealand from five countries in 2004.

question: The line graph shows the percentage of spending in a European country from 1960 to 2000.
content:
The report confers data regarding changes in the volume of spending in a European country between 1960 and 2000 relative to 5 areas - food, leisure, clothing, transport and energy - in the line graph.

In general, people appeared to spend less year by year on food, leisure, clothing - these three held the top spots initially respectively - as well as energy: this area of expenditure had consistently remained at the bottom. However, the money spent on commuting managed to surge, eventually taking over the first spot during the period, with Food and leisure close followers in order.

Changes were somewhat dramatic for the figures for food and leisure as opposed to other categories over the period. Nearly 32% of expenditure was only on food items in 1960, this was as far as down to under 15% in 2000, declining by 5 percentage points at a year-on-year level. Further, leisure formed 20% of total spending in 1960: this was down to nearly 10% in 2000. Unlike the former, it registered a decrease of 5 percentage points during only two decades: from 20% to 15% between 1960 and 1980, and from 1980 to 2000 to 10%.

The opposite pattern of expenditure was observed in clothing and energy, where the decline was accountable for only 5 percentage points throughout the whole period ( from 1960 to 2000). 10% of total expenditure was meant to be spent on clothing in 1960, while a meager 5% on energy: both accounted for 5 percentage lower points by 2000, with the latter group being close to none.

It was the percentage of money spent on transport that exhibited actually an increase. Just under 10% of expenditure was channeled to transport in 1960: a fourth and close spot to clothing. This went up gradually as far as up to 15%, leapfrogging percentages of spending on leisure and food from 1990 to 2000.

content:

question: The line graph below shows the average monthly cost of contracts, in euros, from four mobile network companies in a European country from January to September 2012.
content:
The data compares the changes in the volume of average cost of contracts per month, in euros, in 4 mobile network companies - Domo, Lex, Sim TX and Alpha - in a country in Europe between January to September in the year 2012.

Domo offered the highest contract prices throughout most of the period, starting at 15 euros in January. The contract price surged by nearly 3 euros by March, only to decline in April to around 16 euros. However, it recovered quickly in May, reaching 20 euros, and remained at this level until June. July saw a further increase of 5 euros, after which the price gradually declined to around 18 euros by September, when it was overtaken by Alpha.

Alpha initially offered the lowest prices on the market, at 5 euros from January through June. However, April marked a notable turning point, when the contract price increased sharply to just under 10 euros before returning to its original level by June. From July onwards, Alpha raised its prices significantly, surpassing all three competitors and reaching its peak of 25 euros by September.

Lex demonstrated an overall upward trend throughout the period. In January, its price stood at 13 euros; this declined by 3 euros in February before recovering to 14 euros in March. From then on, prices increased steadily until September, reaching nearly 20 euros—making Lex the third most expensive provider.

Sim TX followed a markedly different trajectory. It ranked third in January at 8 euros per month, maintaining this price until March. From April to June, prices rose significantly to 15 euros, but then declined moderately to 10 euros in July and continued falling to 7 euros by September, making it the cheapest option by the end of the period.

Overall, three companies—Domo, Lex, and Alpha—recorded increasing prices from January to September. Sim TX, however, experienced a reverse trend after its mid-year peak, ultimately offering the lowest monthly cost. Among all four companies, Alpha demonstrated the most dramatic change, rising from the most affordable option for most of the period to rank first by September, closely followed by Domo in second place and Lex in third.

question: The diagram below shows how rainwater is collected for use as drinking water in a town in Australia.
content:
The report provides information about the collection of rainwater in order to use for consumption in a town in Australia.

It all begins during the rain, when rainwater is collected from the roofs of house. As traditionally, rainwater travels through drainage, a sort of a pipe which guides rainwater to the ground, yet it goes underground, where all the water from houses are gathered in one big pipe, and they confront a filter - a device place underground to remove any impurities from rainwater. After then, filtered water follows to a huge storage tank to be collected.

Next to the storage tank is another tank, which serves as a water treatment place. On top this is a device, which releases chemicals to purify the water further and enable it to be ready for consumption. This water continues its journey through a pipe going up to houses to be utilized for household purposes.

Generally speaking, the system of recycling rainwater is rather straightforward and consists of two main phases. Initially, the rainwater is gathered from the roofs of houses and directed to a storage tank under the ground, while going through a water filter. In the second phase, water is treated reportedly in a separate tank before being channeled to households to be consumed.

question: The diagram below shows a simple water filtration system that turns contaminated water into clean drinking water.
content:
The report is about a simple water filtration system that converts contaminated water into clean, drinkable water.

Overall, the water filtration process is straightforward and consists of two main components: a filter tank and a storage drum. The system uses three key filtering materials: sand, charcoal, and gravel.

The water filter assembly begins with a vertical cylindrical tank, which functions as the main filter container and is topped with a plastic lid for protection. The plastic barrel serves as an outer protective layer around the filter tank. Contaminated water is poured into the top of the tank and passes through three distinct layers of filtering materials. From top to bottom, these layers consist of sand, charcoal, and gravel, with the gravel positioned directly above the storage drum.

Once the water has passed through all three layers, it becomes purified and is ready for consumption. The filtered water is then directed through a pipe connected to the bottom of the filter tank into the storage drum, where it is collected and stored for later use.

question: The diagram below shows the process of building an igloo.
content:
The report confers a process of constructing an igloo - a type of shelter made of snow.

In general, stages involved in constructing an igloo is quite straightforward, encompassing overall 2 stages: firstly, assembling a doom out of small and large blocks of ice, and giving some finishing touches,where the ice is the only raw material used in the process.

To begin with, hard-packed snow is sliced into desired forms using a special sawing tool into large and small blocks. Large blocks are laid in a spiraling circular line and leaned inwards to form a doom in the length of 4 meters in 2 layers, after which the other two layers of small blocks are laid. The very top area of an igloo is secured with a circular block of ice placed on the outside.

Afterwards, the polishing process of an igloo follows by, as the exterior is loosened with snow: this is when the doom already stands 2 meters still. A doorway is then erected in the form of an arc. Inside of the shelter, air holes are drilled to let built-up CO2 escape and ensure insulation within, and then the shelter is complete.

question: The chart below shows the number of women per 100 men in Africa, Europe, North America, Central America and Oceania in 1995 and 2005.
content:
The report outlines data about the division of females relative to per 100 males in Africa, Europe, North America, Central America and Oceania in the years 1995 and 2005.

In general, Africa and Europe were countries with an upward trend of female population rate during the period, while the reverse was true for Asia, North and Central America, and Oceania. Of a particular note, the most subdued female-to-male ratio was observed in Europe reportedly, whereas Asian female proportion much outnumbered that of males: this country also topped the list in this regard.

Countries that had somewhat more or equal indexes of females compared to males were Asia, North America, Central America, and lastly Oceania: the figure for female-to-male surged too across these areas. Firstly, Asian female population rate was significantly higher than males, with 105.3 females to per 100 males in 1995, but this was followed by a decrease of 0.4 points in 2005. Oceania, while coming in second, saw a relatively moderate decline, from 103.9 to 99.8 females being equal to 100 males. In 1995, female population rate was almost on match with that of males in 1995 in North and Central America, following in third and fourth respectively (100.1 and 100 females recorded per 100 males). These figures were down to 96.9 in North America and 97.5 in Central America in 2005.

The number of women for every 100 men rose, at varying degrees, in Africa and Europe. The difference in the gender composition of the population has shrunk from 1995 to 2005, increasing from 97.8 to 99.2 females for every 100 males. Europe followed the suit, though there were less women per 100 men, starting at 89.4 and rising to 92.8 in 2005.

question: The chart below shows the composition of family and non-family households in a North American country between 1970 and 2003.
content:
The data looks at the composition of two types of households - family and non-family - in a country in The North America between 1970 and 2003.

As can be seen, there was a universal upward trend in the share of all sorts of households in the country during the period in question, with the notable exception of households of married-couple households - it remained by far the most popular category. In contrast, single fathers with children appeared to be the least common type of household by 2003 - originally non-family households held this position.

There were 4 types of family households: married couples, single fathers with children, single mothers with children, and other member sharing - in 1970. From which, 61% was married-couple households, representing the largest share by a considerable margin. The share of other member sharing followed in a distant second, making up 13%. This was 3 percentage points more than that of single mothers with children. In that year, single fathers living with children formed 9% of the total share, making it the rarest sort of household.

The total share of non-family households was accountable for 7% in 1970. This was split evenly among individuals living along and those sharing rooms (4% vs 3%).

By 2003, all family households categories had enjoyed modest growth, where the percentage of married couples was a notable exception. This particular type of household remained prevalent, though it dropped from 61% to 41%. However, single mother and father households living with children registered an increase of one percentage point, to 10% and 9% respectively, while the percentage of other member sharing surged by 2 percentage points.

There was relatively gradual growth in the proportion of non-family households. The percentage of single-person households rose markedly by 9 percentage points, to 13%: This was a point higher than that of room sharing category, which accounted for 11%.

question: The chart below shows the number of international visits made by UK residents for five different reasons from 1994 to 1998.
content:
The report is about the volume of international visits by UK residents relative to 5 reasons of visit in 5 consecutive years, from 1994 to 1998.

Generally speaking, there was a general upward trend in visits abroad during the period in question, where those travelling for holiday reasons represented the most pronounced growth, as well as the largest number: This was followed by business visits in second and visits to friends and relatives in third respectively. In stark contrast, visits for other reasons remained the least significant during the period.

Travelers cited holiday visits as their primary reason reportedly from 1994 to 1998, starting with 15246 visits made in this purpose in 1994. This, however, was down 348 visits the next year, which quickly recovered and surged to 17 896 visits in 1996. By 1998, the figure had hit over 20 000 visits, making it the chart-peak result (20700). Another common reason stated by UK citizens was business visits: there were 3155 visits made in 1994 due to this reason. The amount of business visits negligibly rose from 1995 to 1998,reaching 3957 visits in 1998.

Paying a visit to friends and relatives ranked third. Around 2689 visits were made in 1994 in this regard, after which it was on an upward trend till 1996, up to 2774. In 1997, the number hit over 3000, and increased to 3181 in 1998.

In comparison, other unspecified reasons were the least popular reason for international visits by UK citizens, where only 982 visits were recorded in 1994. This number once showed a decline of 86 visits in 1995, and this was up to 1030 and 1054 visits, respectively in 1995 and 1996. Yet, the number again declined to 990 in 1998.

In general, there was made visits at 22072 in 1994, 21 610 in 1995, and 24 949 in 1996. Notably, the number of total visits became noticeable in 1997 and 1998 (27 447 vs 28 828).

question: The chart below shows the employment patterns of men and women aged 18 to 34 in Australia from 1976 to 2011.
content:
The report examines information about employment patterns of males and females aged between 18 and 34 in Australia from 1976 to 2011.

Overall, there was a general downward trend in the employment rates across both genders during the period in question. However, male employment rates substantially outpaced female employment, despite a marked decline in male employment over the years. Notably, younger women demonstrated higher employment participation in Australia, whereas peak male employment occurred among older age groups.

Examining employment patterns by gender in 1996, approximately 55% of men aged 18 were employed, compared to 50% of women in the same age group. Employment rates increased substantially for men, reaching nearly 70% by age 22, whereas female participation exhibited a modest decline to approximately 45% at this age. As men approached their 30s, employment rates stabilized around 70%, before climbing sharply to approximately 80% at age 30. Conversely, female employment rates declined modestly by 10 percentage points to 40% at age 25, subsequently edging down until age 34, where they reached approximately 10%.

By 2011, employment rates for both genders had declined, albeit at differing extents. Male employment underwent a steeper decline, commencing at approximately 40% for those aged 18. By age 24, this had surged to approximately 55%. Male employment then fluctuated around 55% between ages 23 and 28, before rising sharply to over 70% at age 34. Female employment followed the suit, beginning at roughly 50% and declining by 5 percentage points between ages 19 and 23. Employment rates then recovered, rising to approximately 50% by age 25 - unlike the result of 1996. Subsequently, female employment declined marginally to approximately 10% at age 33, mirroring the pattern observed in 1996.

question: The plans below show the proposed changes to the layout of an office.
content:
The pictures illustrate some future changes into the layout of an office.

Overall, the traditional layout of the office is expected to witness some significant changes, including the introduction of meeting and outdoor seating areas which will come at the expense of greenery. Plus, there is forecast to be a huge change in the arrangement of rooms.

At present, the office includes overall 7 rooms along with a bathroom. The entrance is located in the southeast corner of the building, to the opposite of which is a bathroom in the corner, while a reception is placed near the entrance. To the left of the entrance, 4 office rooms are based in order. There are a stock room, a canteen, and a kitchen located in order of from-east-to-west to the right of the main corridor.Moreover, the office building features two grasslands on both west and east sides.

According to the future plan, access is planned to be relocated to a more central location as well as the reception,where two office rooms around the entrance will be enlarged. The kitchen and canteen are expected to be converted into office rooms. The stock room, however, will remain intact. Another change is predicted to be a construction of an outdoor seating area. This will take place of the grassland on the west side, while a new meeting area will emerge instead of the other grassland. The latter redevelopment is planned to include a small coffee area and a bathroom.

question: The plans below show a school in 1985 and at present.
content:
The report outlines changes implemented into the layout of the school, featuring it in 1985 and at present.

The original school layout used to have access from the main road to the north, with the entrance located in the northwest and exit in the northeast,forming a Y-shape configuration. A parking lot was situated in the middle of these roads,with a junction leading to a playing field that occupied the entire southern region. Immediately to the left of the entrance stood the school office, with the library adjacent to it, while a smaller additional car park and a classrooms facility were positioned to the opposite of the library. Another classrooms block could be seen on the other side of the road - this featured two storeys. This version could accommodate 1 ,500 students.

Following redevelopment, the school now has the capacity to cater for a total of 2 300 students. The road has been converted from its Y-shape to an U-form, while the library has made room for a center for learning resources and a computer room, and the small car park has been demolished entirely. The single-story classrooms block has been relocated further south, with an introduction of facilities beneath it - a fitness center and a swimming pool - coming at the expense of the playing field. There is now additional classrooms block below of a 3 story classroom block, which was originally 2 stories. The playing fields have shrunk considerably, as the new above mentioned facilities emerged.

In summary, the school has witnessed a major transformation, with several brand-new facilities appearing in the layout. These, while coming at the cost of the playing field area,have improved the overall functionality of the campus.These changes, in turn, have made the school more student-friendly, and it can now serve a noticeably larger amount of students.

question: The line graph below shows carbon emissions, in million tonnes, from gas, oil and coal from 1990 to 2010.
content:
The report compares the volume of produced carbon emissions,in million tones, from three fossil fuels - gas, oil, and coal - from 1990 to 2010.

Overall,gas generated the most significant volume of carbon emissions by the end of the period, while oil and coal emitted substantially lower amounts. The former also registered an overall increase over the years, whilst the reverse is true for other types of fossil fuels.

Coal was the largest carbon dioxide emitter in 1990, accounting for just above 300 million tones.However, emissions were down 50 million tones in the next interval and kept on reducing negligibly until 2010, where coal was responsible for as approximately as 200 million tones of carbon, ranking third by the end of the period.

Oil represented the second major source of carbon emissions, the result of which made up about 270 million tones of carbon in 1990. Emission levels fluctuated around this amount until 2005 before declining moderately to 210 million tones,finishing in second place.

Although starting as lowest carbon emitter, gas demonstrated the most drastic transformation. In 1990, gas was producing at around 200 million tones of carbon, but this amount moderately increased by approximately 50 million tones in each five-year interval until 2000. From that point on, it had slowly surged to 320 million tones of carbon by 2010 - the highest level recorded across all three fuels - establishing gas as the leading carbon emitter.

question: The line graphs below show changes in the UK steel industry from 1970 to 2000: demand, production, imports and employment.
content:
The line graphs illustrate changes in the UK steel industry from 1970 to 2000, examining demand, production, import levels, and employment figures.

In general, The domestic demand consistently exceeded both production and import levels. While The country recorded a pronounced increase in import levels, there was a downward trend in both production and demand rates during the period in question. Notably, The steel industry also saw a drastic decline in employment rates over the years.

Focusing on value changes in the industry, the total UK demand for steel made up 200 000 million tonnes in 1970. This went down gradually until 1980, reaching around 180 000 million tonnes,after which the trend continued declining at a moderate level to nearly 100 000 million tones until 1990. From then onwards, the figure for total demand was relatively stable, closing at 100 000 tonnes in 2000. The trend for the UK production rate followed the suit, dipping from 150 000 million tones in 1970 to about 80 000 million tones in 1990. By 2000, the UK production rate mirrored the trend for total demand, remaining stable at 80 000 million tones. In contrast, The index of import rate for steel demonstrated a drastic increase, which started at approximately 10 000 million tones in 1970. This was on a gradual upward trend until 2000, hitting nearly 100 000 million tonnes by the end of the period.

With regards to employment changes in the industry, 50 000 workers were employed in the industry in 1970. The figure then declined moderately to 40 000 in 1980, followed by another similar change until 1990, albeit at a noticeable degree to 20 000. By the end of the period, the total employment figure in the steel industry accounted for 18 000.

content:

question: The chart below shows the total sales of a pharmaceutical company in four regions between 2002 and 2006.
content:
The report outlines information about changes in the total sales of a drug company, in percentage terms, relative to 4 regions - Asia, Europe and Africa, North America, and South America - between 2002 and 2006.

In general, the leading countries in terms of the most significant proportion of sales were Europe along with Africa, whereas the reverse was true for South America. It was Asia that enjoyed a general upward trend throughout the period, while the figures for Europe and Africa, and North America were on a downward slope. Focusing on countries with the highest sale rates, 44% of total sales was made in Europe and Africa, the result of which edged up to 45% in 2003. North America ranked second in the ranking of countries with the most sales, starting at 33% in 2002. From then on, there was observed a gradual reduction until 2005, hitting 21%. In 2006, the figure for North America’s sales levelled off at its former result.

Remaining countries made up relatively smaller percentages of sales. Asia and South America followed in third and fourth in terms of sale rates (12% vs 11%). From 20% in 2003, the figure for Asia registered an interval-on-interval growth of 2% until 2005, reaching 24%. After this, it had climbed to 28% by 2006, becoming the second country with the highest sales and exceeding North America. However, the South America’s share of sales reduced moderately in 2003 and 2004 (7% and 6% respectively), which recovered to its initial percentage the next interval and was stable until the end(11%).

content:
The bar chart compares European young people's expectations of change across 5 areas - health, air quality, water quality, food quality, and people communication - over the next 20 years.

Overall, people communication is the only category where the majority expects improvement, whereas air quality stands out as the area viewed most negatively. Meanwhile, opinions on the other three areas are fairly evenly split, tilting slightly toward "get worse."

question: The maps below show the development of a town called Brindell and its surrounding area in 1800, 1900 and 2000.
content:
The diagrams illustrate how a town called Brindell and its surrounding areas developed across three points in time: 1800, 1900, and 2000.

Overall, the most significant development occurred in the south-eastern part of the map, where farmland was converted into an industrial zone and a residential area was added. In contrast, the western side remained largely unchanged throughout the period, while a public park was established on the southern edge of the woodland.

In 1800, a river called Stour stretched from west to east across the layout. Brindell town was situated in the north-western part, while animal farmland occupied the south-eastern area. A crop farmland was located in the upper western region, with a woodland to its right.

By 1900, there had been little significant development overall. However, the animal farmland in the south-east had been converted into an industrial zone. Alongside this, a workers' village called Bun Hill emerged to the right of the industrial area.

By 2000, further changes had taken place. The industrial zone expanded in size, and a public park was built on the southern edge of the woodland for the residents of Bun Hill. All other areas of the layout remained intact throughout the period.
